 Lauren Anderson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 10:13 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Connor Wood's Dad Texts Walgreens Instead of Voting for Him on DWTS: A Hilarious Mix-Up Connor Wood has one very dedicated supporter on his side during his Dancing With the Stars journey , even if his dad's voting efforts haven't exactly gone according to plan.
 The social media personality recently found himself at the center of a hilarious family mix-up when his dad accidentally texted Walgreens 10 times while attempting to vote for him on DWTS . As it turns out, the pharmacy chain's phone number and the show's voting number are just one digit apart, making it all too easy to send a message to the wrong recipient.
 The mishap has since become a memorable part of Wood's experience on the competition series, giving fans another glimpse into the family support behind his ballroom journey.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But now, the funny story is getting a sweeter follow-up.
 Wood is set to dedicate his performance on tonight's episode to his dad, bringing him onto the ballroom floor for a special father-son moment . After his dad's determined (if slightly misguided) attempt to help him earn votes, the tribute offers Wood a chance to celebrate the person cheering him on throughout the competition.
 The mix-up has also given fans a particularly relatable reminder that even the most well-intentioned support can go hilariously wrong. In this case, the difference between helping a loved one stay in the competition and accidentally contacting a pharmacy came down to a single digit.
 For Wood, the story is becoming more than just a funny anecdote about his dad's texting habits. As he prepares to share the ballroom with him, the moment offers an opportunity to turn a viral family mishap into something more meaningful.
 Advertisement Advertisement And while his dad may have had a little trouble getting his votes to the right place, there's no question about where his support lies.
